name: handler_txtprogressbar
title: Progression Handler: Progress Reported as Plain Progress Bars (Text) in the Terminal

origin.description: Report progress with a utils text progress bar in the terminal.
origin.usage: handler_txtprogressbar(char = "=", style = 3L, file = stderr(), intrusiveness = getOption("progressr.intrusiveness.terminal", 1), target = "terminal", ...)

arguments.name: char
arguments.text: The symbol that forms the bar. ANSI color is kept in the symbol. The width is measured after that color is removed. The default is "=".

arguments.name: style
arguments.text: The utils txtProgressBar style, 1, 2, or 3. The default is 3.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: An open connection. The default is stderr().

arguments.name: intrusiveness
arguments.text: How disruptive the reporter is. The default is the option progressr.intrusiveness.terminal, or 1.

arguments.name: target
arguments.text: Where progress is rendered. The default is "terminal".
Further named arguments. make_progression_handler arguments stay on the handler. The rest are passed to txtProgressBar.

origin.details: A bar is created on initiate unless the handler is disabled or times is 1. A sticky message is erased, printed, and the bar is drawn again. clear TRUE erases the bar and sends the closing newline to a temporary file, which is then deleted. clear FALSE draws the bar at max_steps and leaves that newline on the connection. max equal to min is a void bar, which erase and redraw skip.
origin.example:
path <- tempfile("txt")
con <- file(path, open = "wt")
handler <- handler_txtprogressbar(style = 3L, file = con, enable = TRUE, clear = FALSE)
with_progress({
  p <- progressor(steps = 4, on_exit = FALSE)
  p(message = "one")
  p(message = "two")
  p(message = "three")
  p(message = "four")
}, handlers = handler, enable = TRUE, interval = 0, delay_terminal = FALSE, delay_stdout = FALSE, delay_conditions = character())
close(con)
n <- nchar(readChar(path, file.info(path)$size, useBytes = TRUE))
cat("handler_txtprogressbar wrote ", n, " characters for four steps.\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Report progress with the utils text progress bar.

arguments.name: char
arguments.text: The symbol that forms the bar. ANSI color is kept in the symbol. The width is measured after that color is removed. The default is "=".

arguments.name: style
arguments.text: The utils txtProgressBar style, 1, 2, or 3. The default is 3.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: A text stream with write(). The default is sys.stderr. An empty string is stdout.

arguments.name: intrusiveness
arguments.text: How disruptive the reporter is. The default is the option progressr.intrusiveness.terminal, or 1.

arguments.name: target
arguments.text: Where progress is rendered. The default is "terminal".

arguments.name: extra
arguments.text: Further named arguments. make_progression_handler arguments stay on the handler, including enable and clear. The rest are passed to txtProgressBar.

translation.details: A bar is created on initiate unless the handler is disabled or times is 1. A sticky message is erased, printed, and the bar is drawn again. clear true erases the bar and sends the closing newline to a temporary file, which is then deleted. clear false draws the bar at max_steps and leaves that newline on the stream. max equal to min is a void bar, which erase and redraw skip.
translation.example:
import os
import tempfile

from progressr.bars import handler_txtprogressbar
from progressr.evaluate import with_progress
from progressr.progressor import progressor

path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "txt.txt")
handle = open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
handler = handler_txtprogressbar(style=3, file=handle, enable=True, clear=False)

def body():
    progress = progressor(steps=4, on_exit=False)
    progress(message="one")
    progress(message="two")
    progress(message="three")
    progress(message="four")

with_progress(body, handlers=handler, enable=True, interval=0, delay_terminal=False, delay_stdout=False, delay_conditions=())
handle.close()
n = len(open(path, "rb").read().decode("utf-8"))
print(f"handler_txtprogressbar wrote {n} characters for four steps.")
